decisions: User request: fix three gaps found while planning hackathon Day 10 (a factory diagram with verification gates): (1) no required checks ran on pull requests, (2) nothing verified post-merge paperwork (on PR 21 the body said '(#20)' instead of 'Closes #20' so the issue stayed open, and BACKLOG.md said 'done (issue #20)'), (3) the label-triggered bot lane skipped the ticket investigation and the local review. The user asked 'fix it?'; the design below is the coding agent's.

Agent choice: ticket-link reads ticket ids (T-NNN) from the pull request title only. The body often mentions other tickets in passing ('section names moved to T-027'), and bot branch names are not trusted. Known limit, written in AGENTS.md: a ticket PR without the id in its title is not checked.

Agent choice: the BACKLOG.md row must say exactly 'done (PR <this number>)' before the merge. This needs a follow-up commit after the PR is opened, because the number is not known earlier. Accepted cost: the check is red until then.
Agent choice: BACKLOG.md cells are compared as written, without trimming (project rule 6, Validate Before You Normalize). A status with stray spaces fails on purpose.

Agent choice: the Investigation guard in agent-ticket.yml checks only that the section heading exists in the issue body, not its content. The human who adds the label has read it. Written as a known limit in journal/day-10.md.

Agent choice: the bot's Qodo review step is opt-in through a QODO_API_KEY repository secret. Without the secret, or when 'qodo whoami' fails, the lane behaves as before ('Implemented, gate pending'). The installer URL and SHA-256 are Qodo's published immutable pin for the POSIX installer; the checksum is verified before the script runs.

Agent choice: scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts writes to stdout/stderr itself. The AGENTS.md convention that only src/cli.ts touches process streams is about the product library under src/; scripts/ is factory tooling. The pure function checkPrTicket does no I/O.
Agent choice: check.yml runs on pull_request 'edited' too, so that fixing the PR body reruns ticket-link.
Branch protection on main (making the three check names required) is a repository setting left to the human, to be turned on after check.yml is on main. Not part of this diff.

Agent choice for finding aad38bfd: an issue is the ticket's own when its title names the ticket id (every issue in this repository is titled "T-NNN: ..."). The script asks the GitHub REST API for the title of each issue the body closes, through an injectable IssueLookup; tests pass a fake, so no test uses the network (rule 5). A number that is a pull request, or a 404, is not an issue. A failed lookup is exit 2, never a pass. Extra closed issues that belong to no ticket are allowed.
Agent choice for finding 0cc845e7: two BACKLOG.md rows for one ticket are a problem regardless of their statuses.

Agent choice for finding 8e3e55d2: the Investigation guard removes the ready-for-agent label itself so that adding it again fires a new labeled event; if removal fails, the comment tells the human to remove and re-add it. The workflow only listens to labeled, so the removal starts nothing.

Agent choice for finding 7626e3f0: every failure of the Qodo setup step (download, checksum, installer, version, sign-in) ends the step successfully with available=false and a warning naming the stage. A script whose checksum does not match is never run.

Finding 47242917 (ticket-link passes an issue-reading GITHUB_TOKEN to a script from the pull request): DISPUTED by the agent, waiting for the human. Evidence: (1) on a pull_request event GitHub runs the workflow file from the pull request's merge commit, so the author of a pull request already controls every step that runs with this token; moving the lookup out of the script into a workflow step would not keep the token from them. (2) The job asks for contents: read and issues: read on a public repository, so the token reads nothing an anonymous request cannot read; for pull requests from forks GitHub issues a read-only token regardless. (3) An anonymous request is not used because it is rate-limited per runner address, which would make a required check flaky. The reasoning and its limit (a private repository or a write scope would need a redesign) are written in check.yml above the permissions block. The agent did not change the design and does not dismiss the finding; the human decides.

Fix for finding 1c731999 (the agent run could read QODO_API_KEY): the whole optional Qodo review step was removed from agent-ticket.yml: no installer, no key in the action environment, no qodo tool for the agent. The label lane ends with Implemented, gate pending, as before Day 10, and the quality gate is applied on the pull request. Agent choice; the gap (no Qodo review before the bot commits) is recorded as still open in journal/day-10.md and in the workflow header. This also removes the untested installer path that finding 7626e3f0 and the reviewer comment were about.

Fix for finding fc8fffff: closing keywords are matched only in rendered text. New scripts/markdown-text.ts visibleText() drops HTML comments, fenced code blocks and, for this check, inline code spans. Indented code blocks are not recognized; documented in the function comment. When in doubt the helper hides more, which makes the check stricter, never looser.

Fix for finding e4ed609b: the Investigation guard moved from a grep in the workflow to scripts/ticket-ready.ts with tests/ticket-ready.test.ts (function tests and child-process tests). The guard step now runs after checkout and setup-node; an issues event checks out the default branch, so the script is the one on main. The section must also be non-empty. The checksum branch named in the finding no longer exists.

Finding d2451e51 (a title naming an earlier ticket, e.g. "(T-027, split from T-008)", cannot pass) is informational: reported to the human and left unchanged, as the project gate says for Low findings. The agent agrees it is real.
Reviewer comment applied: check.yml cancels in-progress runs only for pull requests; runs on main have one concurrency group per commit.

USER DECISION for findings bb44ea06 and 49bf2faa (factory scripts touch process streams outside src/cli.ts): the human chose to amend the rule, not the code. Asked through a prompt with three options (amend the rule; move the checks into src/cli.ts as subcommands; keep both and dismiss), answered: Amend the rule. AGENTS.md, Code conventions, now reads: under src/, cli.ts is the only module that may touch process.stdout, process.stderr or process.exitCode; factory scripts under scripts/ touch the process only in their entry block at the end of the file, and every function in them returns values or throws. scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts and scripts/ticket-ready.ts follow this: run() returns code, stdout and stderr; only the entry block writes. The rule in Qodo Review Standards (4522070) still has the old text until the rules are re-imported after the merge, which is a manual step for the human.

Fix for finding 823561fb (a ticket PR whose title has no T-NNN skipped the check): a pull request is now a ticket PR when its title names a ticket OR its body closes an issue whose title starts with a ticket id. PRs 7, 12, 14 and 16 had titles with only an issue number; they would now be checked. Remaining limit, written in AGENTS.md: a PR that neither names a ticket nor closes a ticket issue is not checked; the check catches slips, not deliberate bypass.

Fix for finding 48562f07: an issue belongs to a ticket only when its title starts with the id and a colon (T-008: ...). A mention further into the title does not count. All six existing issues of the repository are titled that way; AGENTS.md now asks for it.

Fix for finding c6db41d9: for the closing-keyword check, lines indented by four spaces or a tab are ignored. This also hides a continuation line deep inside a list; accepted, because it only makes the check stricter.

Findings 8b2a81e1 and c51f36de (ticket-ready rejects an indented heading; a section that starts with a sub-heading or a bold label is read as empty) are informational: reported to the human and left unchanged, as the project gate says for Low findings. The agent agrees both are real; the ticket format uses the bold label followed by prose, which passes.

Reviewer comments applied: ticket-link is now its own workflow (.github/workflows/ticket-link.yml) so that editing a PR title or body does not rerun or cancel the test jobs; AGENTS.md says the check catches slips, not intent. Not applied: an opt-out for titles that mention an earlier ticket (finding d2451e51, informational, reported).
notes:
Scope of this review: .github/workflows/check.yml (new), .github/workflows/agent-ticket.yml (modified), scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts (new), tests/pr-ticket-check.test.ts (new), AGENTS.md, BACKLOG.md, tsconfig.json. Excluded on purpose: journal/, evidence/, and tickets/T-028-source-hygiene.md, which belongs to a different ticket and pull request.

Verified: 'npm run check' on Windows, Node 24: typecheck clean, tests 222, pass 222, fail 0 (165 before this change; 10 of the 203 are tests/source-hygiene.test.ts from another ticket, outside this review). The new tests were written first and failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before the script existed. The PR 21 title and body are one of the failing cases.

NOT verified: no workflow has been run. The YAML files were not parsed by any tool on this machine (no YAML parser available). The tests have never run on Linux; check (ubuntu-latest) will be their first Linux run. The agent-ticket.yml changes are untested: whether the Qodo installer works non-interactively on a runner, whether 'qodo whoami' accepts QODO_API_KEY plus QODO_BASE_URL from the environment, whether anthropics/claude-code-action passes step env to the agent's shell, and whether 'qodo review' works in a fresh runner clone. Testing them needs a label and a secret, which only the human may add.

Constraints: zero runtime dependencies (rule 4); tests touch no network and no live repository (rule 5): the child-process tests read the repository's own BACKLOG.md from disk and rely on its T-001 row having the status 'done'. PR title and body are untrusted input: they reach the script through environment variables and are never printed back; the BACKLOG status that is printed goes through visible(), which escapes everything outside printable ASCII, so a status cannot forge a line or a workflow command.

Project quality gate (AGENTS.md): action_required and remediation_recommended findings must be fixed when valid; informational findings are reported and left unchanged.

Round 2 verification: the checksum-mismatch path of the Qodo setup step was simulated offline with bash -e: exit 0, available=false, script not run. The label removal and the GitHub issue lookup against the real API were not run. Files outside this review also changed in the working tree for ticket T-028 (scripts/source-hygiene.ts, tests/source-hygiene.test.ts, src/gitlog.ts, tests/gitlog.test.ts, README.md); they are excluded here on purpose and get their own review.

Round 3 verification: the new tests for fc8fffff and e4ed609b were run before the fixes and failed (evidence/day10/red-gapfix-round2.txt: 4 failing of 32). scripts/ticket-ready.ts was run against the real ticket tickets/T-028-source-hygiene.md: exit 0. Still not run: any workflow, the label removal, and githubIssueLookup against the real GitHub API.

Round 4 verification: the new tests for 823561fb, 48562f07 and c6db41d9 were run before the fixes and failed (evidence/day10/red-gapfix-round3.txt: 12 failing of 37, including existing tests whose expected text changed). This is the review after the third and last fix round the project gate allows.
